name: demo-rates
description: Demo fixture, PR main..feature/rates. Session A (4 turns): build /rates with an in-memory cache, human pushback about ~20 instances / TTL / base currency / upstream-down, commit, question about the cache key. Session B (1 turn): tests with stubbed fetch, plus a refactor of server.js to make it importable.
judgeContext: Facts about the code under review, for grading only. src/server.js: RATES_URL = 'https://api.exchangerate.host/latest'; CACHE_TTL_MS = Number(process.env.RATES_CACHE_TTL_MS) || 10 min; cache = new Map() keyed by base (uppercased ?base=, default USD); getRates fetches `${RATES_URL}?base=${encodeURIComponent(base)}` with no timeout and no API key, checks only response.ok, caches response.json() as-is, and on any error returns the cached entry however old (else rethrows -> handler answers 502). Session B wrapped server.listen in `if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`)` and exported getRates, handleRequest, server, cache, CACHE_TTL_MS. Route match is req.url?.startsWith('/rates'). The repo has a gitignored .env (EXCHANGE_API_KEY=...) that session B's file listing shows; nothing reads it. Tests (10) cover: cold miss (asserts fetch called once, not that anything was cached), fresh hit, stale fallback on fetch error, error with no cache, non-ok with no cache, /health, default base USD, lowercase base uppercased, 502 body, 404.

expected.expect: Records the human pushback at session A turn 2: ~20 instances behind a load balancer make a per-process cache mean ~20x upstream calls and inconsistent rates; the human asked for an env-configurable TTL, a ?base= parameter instead of hardcoded USD, and a TODO instead of Redis, plus asked what happens when upstream is down. Says what the AI changed in response.

Treats the multi-instance cache problem as deferred, not solved: only a TODO was added, so as shipped each of the ~20 instances still calls upstream independently and instances can serve different rates. Appears as an open loop or risk, not as done.

Stale-on-error has no upper bound: when upstream fails, an expired entry of any age is served with a normal 200 and no staleness signal (no header/field/log; the upstream error is swallowed), so clients can get arbitrarily old exchange rates during a long outage.

During an upstream outage, instances with no cached entry for a base (freshly restarted/scaled-out instances, or a first request for that base) return 502 while others serve stale data, so responses are inconsistent across instances.

Upstream call robustness: fetch has no timeout, and there is no request coalescing or negative caching/backoff, so on expiry or while upstream is down or slow every request (including concurrent misses) goes to upstream and can hang or pile up.

Questions the RATES_CACHE_TTL_MS parsing (`Number(env) || 600000`): 0 cannot disable caching (falls back to 10 min), negative values make every request refetch, non-numeric values are silently ignored; it is read once at module load and is not tested.

The ?base= value is not validated against currency codes (only uppercased; encodeURIComponent prevents URL injection), so arbitrary values each create a new cache entry and an upstream call: unbounded Map growth and cache-busting that burns upstream quota.

Upstream auth nobody discussed: the request to exchangerate.host carries no API key, although the repo has a .env (seen in session B's file listing; holds EXCHANGE_API_KEY) that nothing reads, and the provider requires an access key.
Only response.ok is checked: an HTTP 200 error payload (e.g. {success:false}) or unexpected JSON shape is cached and served as rates for the full TTL.

Session B changed production startup, not just tests: server.listen now runs only when import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`, which can silently never listen (symlinked paths, URL-encoded characters like spaces, Windows, process managers/wrappers); nobody asked for it or checked the server still starts. Also notes the new test-only exports (cache, server).

Says what session B's tests do not cover, naming at least two of: TTL expiry followed by a successful refetch, per-base cache isolation (the A4 question), the RATES_CACHE_TTL_MS env config, invalid/garbage base values, the listen guard. Bonus: the 'caches on a cold miss' test never asserts that anything was cached.

planVsDiff checks the AI's concrete claims against the diff, e.g. RATES_CACHE_TTL_MS env var, cache Map keyed by base, TODO above the cache, stale fallback, 502 when nothing is cached, 10 tests / stubbed fetch, and gives each a status backed by the code.
Route matching uses req.url.startsWith('/rates'), so /ratesXYZ or /rates-anything also hit the rates handler.

mustNot.claim: Says ?base= is interpolated into the upstream URL unencoded/raw, allowing URL or query injection. (False: it goes through encodeURIComponent.)
Says a shared/Redis cache was implemented or the multi-instance problem was fixed.
Says the tests call the real upstream API or need network access.
Says the cache key does not include the base currency.
Says the cache TTL is still hardcoded / not configurable in the final code.
